links.outcome: Potential harm in intermediate decisions despite correct final diagnoses, versus final-diagnosis-only scoring
links.effect: 55.2% of hospital trajectories reaching an acceptable final diagnosis passed through a decision with moderate or severe potential harm; 24.8% through a clinically unacceptable one; harm rates 76.2% on MIMIC-IV and 39.6% on ASCENT.
links.quote: A correct final diagnosis does not certify a safe trajectory, and a successful correction does not certify a safe recovery.

Structured corrective feedback versus bare rejection to repair AI errors

links.outcome: unsafe or clinically unacceptable AI decisions
links.effect: 55.2% of acceptable-diagnosis hospital trajectories had moderate/severe potential harm; 24.8% were clinically unacceptable; harm rates were 76.2% on MIMIC-IV and 39.6% on ASCENT.
links.quote: Across 300 cases from a hospital cardiology cohort, MIMIC-IV and the public ASCENT benchmark, with up to seven AI systems per source, 55.2% of hospital trajectories reaching an acceptable final diagnosis passed through a decision with moderate or severe potential harm and 24.8% through a clinically unacceptable one; the harm rates were 76.2% on MIMIC-IV and 39.6% on ASCENT.

links.outcome: error repair and new unsafe decisions
links.effect: Structured corrections resolved 73.6% vs 24.8% after bare rejection; new potentially unsafe decisions followed 30.2% vs 19.7%.
links.quote: Structured corrections resolved 73.6% of first errors versus 24.8% after bare rejection, yet new potentially unsafe decisions followed 30.2% of corrections versus 19.7% of rejections.
